catalog_quote: (27) Languages with exceptional final stress ... Tol (Hokan, Honduras) final if CVC, else penultimate CV (Fleming and Dennis 1977) ... Take an example: in Tol, “in a majority of cases, stress occurs on the final syllable of consonant-final words [phesmás ‘skunk’] and the penultimate syllable of vowel-final words [phésme ‘skunk’] ... However, stress may also occur on the final syllable of vowel final words [?isí ‘water’, chiyó ‘dog’] and, less frequently, on the penultimate syllable of consonant-final words” (Fleming and Dennis 1977, p. 127). Long vowels do not occur, but CV monosyllables are allowed: tI ‘heavy’ p. 121, pi ‘buttocks’, pe ‘rock’ p. 122.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote check: the deciding quotation is verbatim in the Garrett ROA-1031 PDF we hold (sec. 3.3, PDF p.17; record says p.16, off by one), and it is explicitly a carry of Fleming & Dennis 1977:127, which we do not hold. The held Dennis & Dennis 1983 dictionary appendix (p.57) independently confirms the same default as an orthographic rule (unaccented words: final stress if consonant-final, penult if vowel-final; accent written otherwise), so the majority rule is not in doubt. What is thin: (a) the primary 7-page phonology has never been opened by us; (b) two fuller descriptions exist and are unread -- Holt 1999 (60 pp, blurb frames stress as a suprasegmental phoneme with morphological 'shift of stress') and Haurholm-Larsen & Pynes 2024 (44-pp De Gruyter chapter, CrossRef-verified, paywalled, no OA copy found); (c) the tier's own example check found only 3/8 marked polysyllables obeying the rul

sources.quote: 'There are 22 consonant and 6 vowel phonemes in Tol, as well as one suprasegmental phoneme of stress' ... morphological processes include 'vocalic ablaut and apocope, prefixation, infixation, and suffixation, as well as shift of stress'.
sources.note: Publisher blurb calls stress 'one suprasegmental phoneme' and lists 'shift of stress' as a morphological process -- if the sketch treats stress as contrastive rather than edge/closure-predictable, our weight-hedged coding may need to move to lexical-with-default; cited by WALS for Tol but never read by us.
